## Reference Answer
There are multiple ways to see the logs - lets take the example of rebuilding catalogs:

```bash
python3 station_42.py --rebuild_catalog
```

that will display is all the the terminal and you can scroll up. If you want to capture it to a file, you can always do this:

```bash
python3 station_42.py --rebuild_catalog > output.txt
```

which will capture the output and put it in a file called `output.txt`

It also support direct logging to file


```bash
python3 station_42.py -l output.log --rebuild_catalog 
```

Adding the `-v` or `--verbose` option to any of the command above and it will get very very chatty - this can be useful for debugging.

Another option for checking the catalog is to run the `--check_catalogs` option:

 
```bash
python3 station_42.py --check_catalogs
```

Also, just looking at the catalog might tell you what's going wrong:

```bash
python3 station_42.py --printcat STATION_NAME
```
